extracted.intended_audience: NHLBI/NIH grant applicants (PD/PI and Authorized Organization Representative) seeking to appeal an initial peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and standards for applicants (PD/PI and AOR) to submit and support a formal appeal of the NIH/NHLBI initial peer review of a grant application, including allowable bases for appeal, letter requirements, timelines, and Council decision outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of appeals process
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeals process is designed to resolve procedural issues surrounding the initial peer review of an application. The appeals process is used when the issue cannot be resolved administratively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional information on appeals of initial review is in NIH Guide Notices (NOT-97-232, NOT-OD-11-064, NOT-OD-11-101). In most cases it is advantageous to revise and submit a new or resubmission application rather than appeal the initial peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-appeal administrative contact with Program Official (PO)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who is concerned about any procedural aspect of the completed initial peer review of an application should first consider the comments in the summary statement and then contact the appropriate NHLBI Program Official (PO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PO may answer questions about the summary statement and review outcome as well as provide guidance to the applicant. Program Officials may provide guidance about timing considerations related to appealing and other administrative considerations in light of NIH submission policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable bases for appeal (four types of procedural flaws)
rubrics_metrics.description: The four types of procedural flaws related to initial peer review that can form the basis of an appeal are: Evidence of bias on the part of one or more peer reviewers; Conflict of interest, as specified in regulation at 42 CFR 52h.5; Lack of appropriate expertise within the initial peer review committee; Factual error(s) made by one or more reviewers that could have altered the outcome of review substantially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be grounded in one or more of these procedural issues; other issues (e.g., differences in scientific opinion) are not allowable bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal letter signatories and length
rubrics_metrics.description: A valid appeal letter is a clear and succinct written communication (generally three to five pages long) from an institution Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) and the Program Director/Principal Investigator (PD/PI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AOR concurrence is required; a letter that does not include the concurrence of the AOR will not be considered a valid appeal letter. A letter that is determined to be invalid may be returned for revisions so long as the timeframe for a valid appeal letter has not passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal letter substantive requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal letter must describe or explain the reason(s) for the appeal on the basis of a flaw or perceived flaw in the initial peer review of a specific application as specified in one or more of the four allowable issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting information in support of an appeal, applicants are encouraged to identify the page numbers and sections of the application where information is presented. When citing references, the citation number in the application should also be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal letter submission timing and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal letters must be submitted after the summary statement is issued and received at the NHLBI at least 30 calendar days prior to the closed session of the Council meeting to which the application is assigned, in order for NIH staff and Council members to give careful and full consideration to an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If extenuating circumstances prevent a valid appeal letter from arriving 30 calendar days prior to the closed session, such letters may be submitted up to 30 calendar days after the closed session for deliberation at the next Council closed session meeting date. Applicants should consider the possibility that a revision of the letter may be necessary to make the appeal valid and allow sufficient time for revisions to meet the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited bases and contents of appeal letters
rubrics_metrics.description: A typical valid appeal letter does not: cite material that was not in the original application; refer to the review of a prior version of the application; use the locus of review as the basis of an appeal; refer to the cover letter as a basis for appeal; cite concerns or complaints about those policies or procedures regulating initial peer review; cite differences in scientific opinion; appeal the initial peer review of applications submitted in response to Requests for Applications (RFAs); appeal the peer review that follows a Council decision to re-review; include discussions, communications, or both with NIH staff unless it is directly applicable to the procedural flaw related to peer review; respond to the reviewer’s critiques in a manner that is consistent with the introduction section of a resubmission application (A1); request Council to fund the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are explicitly excluded from valid appeals per NIH/NHLBI policy and NIH Notices (e.g., NOT-97-232, NOT-OD-11-064). Appeals of RFA applications and appeals of re-review after Council decision are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity determination and revision opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters addressing the peer review of grant applications are carefully evaluated by senior Institute staff to determine whether the issues raised constitute a valid formal appeal, as defined in NOT-OD-11-064.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A letter that does not meet the criteria and/or does not include the concurrence of the AOR will not be considered valid. A letter determined to be invalid may be returned for revisions that may make it valid, provided the timeframe for a valid appeal letter has not passed. The AOR may elect to withdraw an appeal at any time prior to Council review by submitting an AOR-signed withdrawal letter to the PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative re-review prior to Council consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: If the review staff administratively agree to re-review an application prior to Council consideration, the PO will notify the PI and AOR about the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this occurs, the PI will receive an automatic mailer informing him/her that the application has been reassigned and the assignment will be available in the PI’s NIH eRA commons account. An application is in a pending status until the Council has made a decision on the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on submitting overlapping/similar applications during appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH-wide policy NOT-OD-11-101 states that the NIH will not accept any application that is essentially the same as one currently pending initial peer review unless the applicant withdraws the pending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, while an application is undergoing the appeals process, the applicant may not submit another application with similar science. These applications are considered overlapping applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council decision timeline, possible outcomes, and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant will be notified about Council’s decision within 30 calendar days after Council’s deliberation of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible outcomes of Council review are: concurrence with the decision of the initial peer review group as reflected in the summary statement; or concurrence with the claims presented in the applicant's appeal letter resulting in the recommendation for the deferral for re-review of the unchanged application. Council’s decision concerning resolution of an appeal is final and will not be considered again by the NIH through this or another process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive steps to support fair and appropriate review
rubrics_metrics.description: To facilitate the fair and appropriate peer review of their application, applicants are encouraged to take proactive steps prior to submission and between submission and the initial peer review meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested steps include: contact the appropriate NHLBI PO (listed in the FOA and summary statement) prior to application submission and after the peer review meeting; contact Scientific Review Officers (SROs) with concerns between submission and the review meeting; in the cover letter and conversations with the SRO, identify scientists who may have scientific bias either toward or against the proposed science; in the cover letter, identify potential reviewers who may have either a positive or negative conflict of interest; in the cover letter and follow-up conversations with the SRO, identify specific scientific topic areas (not specific reviewers) of expertise needed to review the application.
